page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the KVM hypervisor platform. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor based on x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The server configuration provides 4 vCPUs sourced from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under dedicated CPU allocation. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-core ratio. Hardware cache specifications include a 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reflect standard entry-tier processing capabilities paired with high memory density. Single-core stress-ng CPU performance measures 1105.68, while multi-core stress-ng reaches 2931.94. Geekbench testing records a single-core score of 920.0 and a multi-core score of 1996.0. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 163.7 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 19.6 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. The system performs 2.83 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 2.28 GB/sec. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

The hardware profile emphasizes memory capacity over high-speed CPU performance, presenting clear tradeoffs for compute-bound tasks. Because benchmark scores place raw CPU and compression throughput in lower performance percentiles, this instance is not designed for heavy mathematical modeling or CPU-intensive compilation. Its high memory-to-core ratio offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-centric workloads that require high buffer capacity without demanding top-tier compute performance. Appropriate workload fits include in-memory key-value stores like Redis, caching layers, lightweight database execution, and memory-buffered web services.
